name: marking-menu

frames.best_why: Frame 3 shows the full radial disc with all eight icons and a highlighted slice.

tagline: Hold and flick in a direction to pick from a ring of icons.
summary: A gesture surface that opens a circular menu of eight destinations around the pointer. Hold still to see the ring, flick a direction to pick blind, or use the Menu button and the arrow keys.
appearance: A dark rounded panel with a small icon and Home label at the top left and a Menu button at the top right, with centred prose inviting a press. Opened, a pale circular disc appears with eight outlined icons spaced evenly around the rim and a small hub in the middle.
behaviour: Pressing and holding for a moment opens the disc at the cursor; moving past a short distance without waiting turns the stroke into a direction-only pick. The slice nearest the pointer highlights and its name appears in the hub; releasing commits the choice and updates the top-left label.
demo_content: Hint asking to press or flick; eight default destinations from Home to Settings.
use_when: Power users repeat the same eight destinations and want one gesture instead of a list to scan.
avoid_when: Discoverability is low: nothing hints at the hold-and-flick gesture, and the Menu button is the obvious path.
customise: Pass up to eight items as an array of id, label and icon, choose the surface through children, and handle picks with onSelect; timing and disc size are constants in the source.
weight_why: Motion springs plus a requestAnimationFrame stroke trail, only while a gesture runs.

a11y.note: The press-and-flick surface is a gesture-only path with no role, so keyboard users must find the small Menu button first.

issues: The hub destination name is low-contrast grey and hard to read against the pale slice.
The demo's closed surface looks near-empty, so the still gives little sense of the gesture.
polish_why: Custom gesture menu with a considered trail and spring; the faint hub label is the flaw.
